raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On HIP, the DeepSeek-V4.1 FP4 prefill indexer builds a schedule for every prefill call with `_prefill_schedule_prep_kernel` (in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/fp4_indexer_schedule_hip.py`) and AITER's `_prefill_cta_info_kernel`. Triton specializes a plain `@triton.jit` kernel on each integer argument (whether it is 1 or a multiple of 16) and on the 16-byte alignment of each pointer, and compiles a new variant for every new combination. Each prefill call brings its own row count, table widths and strides, and `PrefillScheduleBuffers` slices its regions at a stride of exactly the row count, so the pointer alignment changes with the row count too. New variants therefore compile while serving, 0.4-2.8 s for the first call of each one on MI355X. In a short trial of a long-prompt serving benchmark with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4, the prep kernel compiled four times, about 1.5 s each, inside one measured point. With the attention-TP row shard of #48152 the shapes differ per rank, so a compile can run on one rank while the others wait at the all-gather (suggestion 3 of our review there). This PR applies to main on its own.

## Modifications

- `_prefill_schedule_prep_kernel`: `do_not_specialize` for its per-call integers (the two page-table strides, `T`, `P`, `s_max`, the two widths and `pt_tiles_per_row`), and `do_not_specialize_on_alignment` for its row-metadata and page-table pointers. `BLOCK_T` is the only shape key left.
- `PrefillScheduleBuffers`: each row region starts on a 16-byte boundary (the stride is rounded up to 4 int32), and `[safe, total_splits]` stay adjacent at the end, because the prep kernel writes them as one pair. `_prefill_cta_info_kernel` then sees one alignment signature for every row count.
- `warm_prefill_schedule(device)`: compiles the 9 `BLOCK_T` variants (16 to 4,096 rows) and the unaligned-`local_ends` signature once per device, and is skipped during CUDA graph capture. `refresh_low_ratio_prefill_workspaces` in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/low_ratio_backend_hip.py` calls it, so these compiles happen on the first prefill forward instead of while serving.
- Test: `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_indexer_schedule_hip.py` (1 GPU, gfx950). After the warm-up, 10 schedule builds with every row-count residue modulo 4, varied table widths and unaligned row metadata must add no variant to either kernel.

## Accuracy Tests

The diff changes only Triton's specialization keys, the buffer offsets and one warm-up call, not what the kernels compute. `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_indexer_hip.py`, which checks the indexer kernels that use this schedule against reference logits, passes (12 tests). We did not run an end-to-end accuracy test for this PR alone. We ran it on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, MI355X together with #48152 and the fixes we suggest there, against the same build and server config without them (baseline in parentheses):

| Mode | GSM8K | GPQA Diamond | NIAH 64k / 128k |
|---|---|---|---|
| DSpark | 97.1 (97.0) | 87.9 (90.9) | 1.0 / 1.0 (1.0 / 1.0) |
| No speculative decoding | 97.4 (97.0) | 86.9 (86.4) | 1.0 / 1.0 (1.0 / 1.0) |

GPQA Diamond has 198 questions; on this setup a change with bitwise-identical outputs moved it by -2.5 and +1.0 points, so these GPQA differences are run-to-run spread.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel check on one MI355X GPU: after each version's warm-up, 11 schedule builds over every row-count residue modulo 4, with aligned and unaligned `local_ends`. All GPU results come from our ROCm test build of SGLang (an earlier commit with extra DeepSeek-V4.1 HIP patches) with these two commits applied.

| Version | Warm-up compiles (prep / cta_info) | New variants in the 11 builds (prep / cta_info) |
|---|---|---|
| Before this PR | none | 11 / 8 (0.4-2.8 s per first call) |
| First commit only | 9 / 1 | 0 / 7 (0.28 s each) |
| This PR | 9 / 2 | 0 / 0 |

Serving, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, MI355X: prompts of about 92k tokens that share one long prefix, 1,000 output tokens, `--chunked-prefill-size 16384`, seven points from concurrency 1 to 64, with every Triton compile logged (`SGLANG_TRITON_SLOW_COMPILE_THRESHOLD_SECS=0`).

- Without this PR, the prep kernel compiled inside measured points. In a short trial without the row shard it compiled four times (about 1.5 s each) at concurrency 4. In a short trial with the row shard of #48152, one rank alone compiled it (1.6 s) at concurrency 1 while the others waited at the all-gather, and the P99 TTFT of that point rose from 784 to 1,564 ms against the run without the shard.
- With this PR, together with #48152 and our suggested fixes, no schedule kernel compiled inside a measured point in two full runs, with and without speculative decoding.

We did not time the warm-up on its own, and we did not run an end-to-end benchmark of this PR alone.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -38,6 +38,9 @@
 # up to a multiple of 4, plus 4 more for the scheduler's one-chunk lookahead.
 _PT_BLOCK = 256
 
+# int32s per 16 bytes, the granularity of Triton's pointer-alignment specialization.
+_I32_PER_16B = 4
+
 
 @triton.jit
 def _pad_page_table_tile(
@@ -62,7 +65,32 @@ def _pad_page_table_tile(
     tl.store(dst_ptr + row * dst_stride + cols, vals, mask=inside)
 
 
-@triton.jit
+# Each call brings its own row count, table widths and strides, and its row metadata
+# sits at offsets that move with the row count; specializing on those values or on
+# 16-byte alignment compiles a new variant mid-serving for every new combination, as
+# AITER notes for its own schedule kernels. BLOCK_T is the only shape key left.
+@triton.jit(
+    do_not_specialize=[
+        "pt_src_stride",
+        "pt_dst_stride",
+        "T",
+        "P",
+        "s_max",
+        "w_src",
+        "w_dst",
+        "pt_tiles_per_row",
+    ],
+    do_not_specialize_on_alignment=[
+        "le_ptr",
+        "chunks_ptr",
+        "incl_ptr",
+        "excl_ptr",
+        "rb_ptr",
+        "ls_ptr",
+        "scalars_ptr",
+        "pt_src_ptr",
+    ],
+)
 def _prefill_schedule_prep_kernel(
     le_ptr,  # [T] int32  local_ends (== c4_seq_lens)
     chunks_ptr,  # [T] int32  out
@@ -251,25 +279,31 @@ class PrefillScheduleBuffers:
 
     def __init__(self, rows: int, device: torch.device):
         self.fused = rows <= MAX_FUSED_ROWS
+        # Every row region and the [safe, total_splits] pair (the prep kernel writes
+        # it as one) start on a 16-byte boundary: AITER's cta_info kernel specializes
+        # on pointer alignment, so a stride of exactly rows would compile a new
+        # variant per rows % 4 while serving.
+        stride = triton.cdiv(rows, _I32_PER_16B) * _I32_PER_16B
         if not self.fused:
-            self.storage = torch.empty(2 * rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+            self.storage = torch.empty(2 * stride, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
             # Identity rows over their whole window; constant across refreshes,
             # so these two dispatches happen once per buffer, not per build.
             self.row_to_batch = self.storage[0:rows]
-            self.local_starts = self.storage[rows : 2 * rows]
+            self.local_starts = self.storage[stride : stride + rows]
             torch.arange(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device, out=self.row_to_batch)
             self.local_starts.zero_()
             self.chunks = self.incl = self.excl = None
             self.safe = self.total_splits = None
             return
-        self.storage = torch.empty(5 * rows + 2, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        tail = 5 * stride
+        self.storage = torch.empty(tail + 2, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
         self.chunks = self.storage[0:rows]
-        self.incl = self.storage[rows : 2 * rows]
-        self.excl = self.storage[2 * rows : 3 * rows]
-        self.row_to_batch = self.storage[3 * rows : 4 * rows]
-        self.local_starts = self.storage[4 * rows : 5 * rows]
-        self.safe = self.storage[5 * rows : 5 * rows + 1]
-        self.total_splits = self.storage[5 * rows + 1 : 5 * rows + 2]
+        self.incl = self.storage[stride : stride + rows]
+        self.excl = self.storage[2 * stride : 2 * stride + rows]
+        self.row_to_batch = self.storage[3 * stride : 3 * stride + rows]
+        self.local_starts = self.storage[4 * stride : 4 * stride + rows]
+        self.safe = self.storage[tail : tail + 1]
+        self.total_splits = self.storage[tail + 1 : tail + 2]
 
 
 def build_prefill_schedule(
@@ -381,6 +415,44 @@ def build_prefill_schedule(
     return guarded_out, buffers
 
 
+_warm_prefill_devices: set = set()
+
+
+def warm_prefill_schedule(device: torch.device) -> None:
+    """Compile every BLOCK_T variant of the fused prefill schedule (one per power of two
+    up to MAX_FUSED_ROWS) and both alignments of its local_ends once per device, so no
+    prefill call compiles one while serving; prefill calls of any row count then reuse
+    these. Skipped inside CUDA-graph capture, which must not record the warm-up
+    launches."""
+    if device in _warm_prefill_devices or torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+        return
+    from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.mqa_logits.pa_mqa_logits_fp4_prefill import (
+        CTA_INFO_WIDTH,
+    )
+
+    def build(rows: int, ends_offset: int) -> None:
+        page_table = torch.zeros((rows, 4), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        ends = torch.ones(ends_offset + rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        build_prefill_schedule(
+            page_table=page_table,
+            local_ends=ends[ends_offset:],
+            cta_info_out=torch.empty(
+                (rows, CTA_INFO_WIDTH), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+            ),
+            parallel_unit_num=rows,
+            max_seq_len=page_table.shape[1] * _KV_BLOCK_SIZE,
+        )
+
+    rows = 16
+    while rows <= MAX_FUSED_ROWS:
+        build(rows, 0)
+        rows *= 2
+    # A request group or a row share starts at any row, and AITER's cta_info kernel
+    # keys on whether local_ends is 16-byte aligned.
+    build(16, 1)
+    _warm_prefill_devices.add(device)
+
+
 # Rows per block of the decode prep kernel's loops: its registers stay fixed as the
 # batch grows, where AITER's varctx kernel holds every row in one tile.
 _DECODE_ROW_BLOCK = 1024

@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+"""The HIP FP4 prefill schedule compiles no Triton variant while serving: after warm_prefill_schedule, prefill calls
+of any row count, table width and row-metadata offset reuse the warmed variants."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_gfx95_supported, is_hip
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=20, stage="stage-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+
+def _aiter_fp4_indexer_available() -> bool:
+    if not (is_hip() and is_gfx95_supported()):
+        return False
+    try:
+        from aiter.ops.flydsl import flydsl_pa_mqa_logits_fp4_prefill  # noqa: F401
+    except ImportError:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _aiter_fp4_indexer_available(), "gfx950 with aiter's FlyDSL FP4 indexer"
+)
+class TestPrefillScheduleCompilesBeforeServing(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_no_new_variant_after_warm_up(self):
+        from aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels.mqa_logits.pa_mqa_logits_fp4_prefill import (
+            CTA_INFO_WIDTH,
+            _prefill_cta_info_kernel,
+        )
+
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4 import fp4_indexer_schedule_hip as sched
+
+        kernels = (sched._prefill_schedule_prep_kernel, _prefill_cta_info_kernel)
+        if not all(hasattr(kernel, "device_caches") for kernel in kernels):
+            self.skipTest("this Triton keeps no per-device kernel cache")
+
+        def variants():
+            return [
+                sum(len(entry[0]) for entry in kernel.device_caches.values())
+                for kernel in kernels
+            ]
+
+        device = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
+        sched.warm_prefill_schedule(device)
+        warm = variants()
+        # every row-count residue, table widths and row metadata at unaligned offsets,
+        # as a row share or a request group produces them
+        for rows, width, start in (
+            (17, 5, 0),
+            (102, 37, 3),
+            (333, 1440, 1),
+            (1000, 23, 2),
+            (2047, 64, 0),
+            (2049, 9, 5),
+            (3001, 730, 7),
+            (3002, 12, 4),
+            (4095, 4, 1),
+            (4096, 1441, 0),
+        ):
+            table = torch.zeros(
+                (start + rows, width), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+            )[start:]
+            ends = torch.randint(
+                1, width * 64, (start + rows,), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+            )[start:]
+            units = max(rows, 1024)
+            sched.build_prefill_schedule(
+                page_table=table,
+                local_ends=ends,
+                cta_info_out=torch.empty(
+                    (units, CTA_INFO_WIDTH), dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+                ),
+                parallel_unit_num=units,
+                max_seq_len=width * 64,
+            )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        self.assertEqual(variants(), warm)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
